title: The Empty Display Case
brief:
Museum am Domplatz, 18:08. The visitors are gone, the doors are locked, and the display case in the Gallery is empty. The gold medal “Morgenstern”, on loan for the major exhibition, has disappeared. The display case sensor recorded the removal to the second: 18:04:00. It does not show who took the medal out.

Four people are still in the building: the historian Max Brandt, the restorer Lina Kern, the photographer Nora Weiss and Oskar Falk, the attendant with the bunch of keys. One of them took the medal with their own hands.

Search the Gallery, Courtyard, Archive, Workshop and Foyer, examine what you find, and question the four. Every find can open up new questions and new leads. You have all the time in the world: questions and examinations cost nothing.

Keep apart what people tell you and what recordings and logs prove. Someone who stays silent is not guilty for that reason, and someone who was in the Gallery earlier in the evening was not necessarily there at 18:04.
challengeQuestion: Who removed the medal from the display case by hand at 18:04?

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Gallery at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: I won't comment on that. Ask someone else.

questionTexts.text: Did Max remove the medal by hand?
questionTexts.answer: Max? No, he didn't.

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Workshop at 18:05?
questionTexts.answer: Yes, at 18:05 I was in my workshop, at my workbench.

questionTexts.text: Was Nora in the Courtyard at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Whether Nora was in the courtyard? I can't tell you that.

questionTexts.text: Do you want to tell me anything about the medal?
questionTexts.answer: I have nothing to say about the medal.

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Gallery at 18:02?
questionTexts.answer: Yes, at 18:02 I was in the gallery, I admit that openly.

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Gallery at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: No! By 18:04 I was long gone from there.

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Courtyard at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Yes, at 18:04 I was standing in the courtyard.

questionTexts.text: Was Lina in the Gallery at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: How should I know? I wasn't there.

questionTexts.text: Was the Courtyard photo shoot filmed in full?
questionTexts.answer: Filmed? I don't know anything about that, you'll have to ask Nora.

questionTexts.text: Was Max in the Courtyard at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Yes, at 18:04 Max was standing with me in the courtyard.

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Courtyard at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Yes, I was in the courtyard taking photos.

questionTexts.text: Was your camera running the whole time during the Courtyard photo shoot?
questionTexts.answer: Yes, the camera ran the whole time. I always leave it running during a shoot.

questionTexts.text: Was Max in the Gallery at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: No, he wasn't in the gallery, he was standing right next to me.

questionTexts.text: Was Lina in the Gallery at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Lina? Hm. I was outside, I can't say for sure.

questionTexts.text: Was Max in the Gallery at 18:02?
questionTexts.answer: Indeed, Mr Brandt was in the gallery at 18:02.

questionTexts.text: Was Max in the Gallery at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Indeed. At 18:04 Mr Brandt was in the gallery, I am quite sure of it.

questionTexts.text: Were you in the Archive at 18:04?
questionTexts.answer: Indeed, I was in the archive at my work.

questionTexts.text: Is there a device in the Archive that records who works there?
questionTexts.answer: Indeed, the archive has a logging device. Whoever works there is recorded in it.

questionTexts.text: Was Lina with you in the Archive at 18:03?
questionTexts.answer: Indeed, Ms Kern came to see me in the archive at 18:03.

publicRules.text: Camera images and logs with timestamps are genuine and synchronized with the display case sensor. Witnesses can be mistaken. A visit at a different time and a silence prove no deed.
Only Max, Lina, Nora and Oskar are possible suspects, and exactly one person took the medal. If three are ruled out, the fourth remains.
The medal was taken at 18:04:00 in the Gallery by a single person with their own hands. Anyone who was demonstrably somewhere else at exactly that second is ruled out.

epilogue:
Lina Kern puts the key on the table. “I only wanted to save it,” she says quietly. During a cleaning in the spring she had damaged the medal and repaired the scratch on her own authority. The lender was due to inspect it the next morning. At 18:03 she had Oskar give her the key, at 18:04 she took the medal out of the display case, and at 18:05 she placed it in the transport case in the Workshop.

Max Brandt was in the Gallery at 18:02, but at the time of the theft he was standing with Nora Weiss in the Courtyard, as the complete footage shows. Oskar Falk was honestly mistaken when he claimed to have seen Max in the Gallery at 18:04: the archive camera shows Oskar himself in the Archive at that very second. The medal lies undamaged in the transport case.
